title: Algeria’s New Bid for Regional Influence
gist: Sabina Henneberg argues Algeria under Tebboune is reasserting regional influence (severing ties with the UAE, military deployment to Niger, diversification and a US opening) but will not mend ties with Morocco or abandon Polisario. She advises Washington to balance Rabat and Algiers and build on early-2026 Western Sahara talks.

insights.claim: Algeria severed diplomatic relations with the UAE in September, apparently over Emirati support for armed groups in North Africa that Algiers considers destabilizing.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: A Gulf-North Africa split affects regional security and investment alignments.

insights.claim: Algeria's rise in influence follows the Hirak protests and the decline of its mediator role; under Tebboune it combines internal repression with a more active foreign policy meant to support its economic agenda.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: Domestic legitimacy drives external assertiveness; regime stability is linked to foreign policy.

insights.claim: Tebboune sent four fighter jets to Niamey in August, the first use of Algeria's 2020 constitutional provision allowing foreign military deployments, to protect Niger's junta from an attempted coup.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: Marks a doctrinal shift from noninterference toward active military backing of allies.
insights.locator: Algiers has made it clear that it intends to secure its backyard

insights.claim: Abu Dhabi funds or arms groups in Sudan and Libya (including Khalifa Haftar's forces), which Algeria sees as fueling turmoil, and Algeria calls Tripoli a red line.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: Libya western-front escalation is a risk factor for oil output and Algerian reaction.

insights.claim: Tebboune's 'new Algeria' stresses self-reliance through localization of industries such as medicine, and in April Algeria secured a deal to import 30,000 US cows for a large dairy farm in the south.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: Algeria is opening to foreign agricultural investment, with US partners positioned to benefit.

insights.claim: Pending agreements with Chevron and ExxonMobil to tap Algerian natural gas would boost export availability to Europe and meet ballooning domestic demand.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: Algerian gas expansion with US majors is a potential supply source for Europe; watch signing and timelines.

insights.claim: Algeria hired a US lobbying firm in 2024, bought an office building near the White House this year, and is discussing direct commercial purchases of US military equipment, indicating US tolerance of its Russia arms relationship.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: US-Algeria defense ties may erode the Russian share of Algerian arms purchases.

insights.claim: Algeria will not abandon the Polisario Front or pressure it to accept Moroccan autonomy, as Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf warned that bypassing self-determination would exacerbate tensions.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: The Western Sahara dispute will constrain Algeria-US-Morocco ties and sustains an Algeria-Morocco arms race.

insights.claim: Henneberg recommends Washington balance its Moroccan partnership with the Algerian opening, encouraging modest steps like resuming direct flights and building on early-2026 talks in which Algeria participated.
insights.speaker: Sabina Henneberg
insights.so_what: US policy likely aims to avoid choosing between Rabat and Algiers.
